intro:
Different causes need different surgery

Even the same "drooping eyes" have different causes. Loose skin alone, a sagging muscle, bulging fat, or weakness in the muscle that lifts the eyelid (ptosis) are all different. When the cause differs, the surgery that is needed differs too.

Facial ageing is also not only a matter of sagging — things hollow out as well. It is now accepted that facial ageing begins not only with descent but with the atrophy that takes volume away. Lifting treatments and filling treatments therefore have to be considered together.

How we work

  1. Identifying the causeWe first distinguish whether the problem lies in skin, muscle, fat or volume.
  2. Choosing the methodWe decide whether to lift, to fill (fat grafting, fillers) or to remove (excision).
  3. Managing recoveryWe look after the skin through recovery after surgery as well.

What sets our plastic surgery apart

A clinic that does not throw fat away

Liposuction, fat grafting and cell-based programmes run on within one clinic. Fat removed from the body can be used again to fill a face that has lost volume.

A wide choice of filling treatments

Micro fat grafting that restores volume with your own fat, autologous filler using your own blood, and conventional fillers and botulinum toxin that improve lines without incision — all can be compared and discussed in one place.

Continuing to skin recovery after surgery

Working with our in-house dermatology practice, skin recovery and after-care continue in the same place. Surgery is not the end; we see you through recovery.

tags.d:
Does any of this sound familiar?
  • people say your eyes look small and your expression closed
  • you have a crease on one side only, so the eyes look uneven
  • the eyelids are thick and make-up will not sit
  • people often say you look sleepy
  • you have to tense your forehead to open your eyes comfortably
Double eyelid surgery — two methods
MethodIn plain termsAdvantages and drawbacks
Suture (non-incisional)Without cutting the skin, sutures fix the inner eyelid to create the creaseThe scar is hard to see. However, it can loosen with time. Mostly used in younger patients
IncisionalThe skin is opened, muscle and skin are tidied, and the crease is createdFat can be removed and the result holds well. However, a surgical mark may remain

Neither is simply better; the right method depends on the state of your eyelids. Anaesthesia is usually local, with sedation added if needed.

If people say you "always look sleepy" — it may be ptosis

Ptosis is a state in which the muscle that raises and lowers the upper eyelid has weakened, so the lid droops and the opening narrows. Creating a crease while leaving ptosis untreated will not give the result you want. If the droop is caused by ptosis, correction for that is needed, and the method is chosen according to the degree of droop and the strength of the muscle.

How recovery goes
2–3 days afterKeep the pillow high and apply cold packs around the eyes. Swelling is at its worst
Day 3–4Sutures are removed. Make-up is possible a day later
About 1 weekYou can return to normal life
2–3 monthsThe crease settles fully. Until then it may look unnatural
Points to be aware of
  • To reduce bleeding and bruising, stop aspirin-type painkillers two weeks before surgery. Bring sunglasses on the day.
  • After ptosis surgery the eyes may not close fully during sleep for a while, which can injure the cornea. Use artificial tears by day and protect the eyes with ointment or tape at night.
  • Where the eyes are very hollow, fat grafting can restore a younger look. Eyelid correction and volume restoration can be discussed together in one clinic.

Does any of this sound familiar?
  • a low bridge makes the face look flat
  • the tip is blunt and broad
  • seen from the side there is a bump midway down the bridge (dorsal hump)
  • the alae are wide and look heavy
  • the nose is deviated to one side

We will be honest with you. Rather than expecting a perfect nose, you are a good candidate where what you want corrected is realistic and specific. Surgery is also better carried out after puberty, once the nose has taken its adult form.

What procedures are there?
ConcernProcedure and method
Low bridgeTo raise the whole nose, your own tissue (bone or cartilage) or an implant is placed. For the tip, your own ear cartilage or the cartilage inside the nose (septal cartilage) is usually used. The site the cartilage is taken from is unaffected functionally and cosmetically
Blunt tipWhere the bridge is fine and only the tip is broad, the tip alone can be corrected. Using your own cartilage, or suturing the tip cartilages together to gather and raise them, are the usual methods
Dorsal humpThe hump at the junction of nasal bone and cartilage is removed
Wide alaeA portion is excised. A small scar remains at the border beneath the ala, and sutures come out at around five days
Deviated noseSurgery to straighten the nasal bone, requiring general anaesthesia and one to two days in hospital. Where the inner wall (septum) is deviated, it is corrected at the same time
How recovery goes
Day 2–3Swelling is at its worst. Bruising can extend around the eyes. Cold packs help
Day 3–4The gauze placed inside the nostrils is removed
Day 5–7The fixing tape and the sutures inside the nose are removed
About 1 weekWashing the face and make-up are possible, and most people return to normal life
2–3 weeksSwelling and bruising subside
About 1 monthBetter not to wear glasses until then. The nose must not be knocked

Swelling drains downwards. Sitting up or taking a gentle walk helps more than lying down.

If you are worried about scars

With an incision inside the nose, no scar is visible externally. The open approach, which cuts the columella, leaves a scar, but it is small and in a place that is not easily seen. Rather than insisting on a method that leaves no scar at all, it is better to choose the method most appropriate to the procedure you need.

What to prepare before surgery

Stop smoking and aspirin-type painkillers two weeks beforehand. Please ask thoroughly at the consultation about the tissue and implant to be used, the surgical method, and the complications that can arise.

Does any of this sound familiar?
  • small breasts mean clothes do not sit well
  • the breasts have become smaller and have dropped after childbirth and breastfeeding
  • very large breasts cause pain in the shoulders, neck and back
  • the nipples are drawn inwards (inverted nipples)
Breast augmentation

Surgery that places an implant in the breast to increase its size. The incision may be in the armpit (the most common in Korea, as the scar is barely visible), in the inframammary fold, or around the areola; anaesthesia is usually general.

ImplantAdvantagesDrawbacks
SalineHarmless to the body if it rupturesThe feel is less soft and it can seem heavier
Cohesive silicone gelExcellent, natural feel; even if the shell is damaged the contents barely leakRegular follow-up examination after surgery is recommended
Complications — know them before you decide
  • Capsular contracture — a fibrous capsule forms around the implant and the breast hardens. In severe cases the shape changes or the implant may have to be removed.
  • Implant rupture — research reports rupture in about 5% of saline implants ten years after surgery. In that case the implant can be removed and replaced with a new one.
  • Sensation may be partly dulled, but it mostly recovers, and augmentation does not interfere with breastfeeding.
Breast reduction and correction of ptosis

Excessively large breasts cause physical problems — back, neck and shoulder pain, and dermatitis in the inframammary fold. Reduction removes excess skin and breast tissue to reduce the size. Where the size is normal but the breast has simply dropped, a mastopexy lifts it.

  • Mammography for breast cancer screening is also performed before surgery. Stop smoking and aspirin for at least two weeks.
  • It is performed under general anaesthesia with one to three days in hospital. The scar is in a position that does not show even in a low-cut top, and fades gradually over several months.
  • Where a very large breast has been reduced, difficulty with breastfeeding can occur. It is better to schedule surgery outside the menstrual period.
Correction of inverted nipples

A state in which the nipple is drawn inwards, seen in about 2–3% of women. It is not only a matter of appearance: it can make hygiene and breastfeeding after childbirth difficult, so functional correction is also worthwhile. It is carried out under local anaesthesia with no hospital stay. After surgery for severe inversion, breastfeeding may not be possible, and recurrence requiring further surgery can occur.

Does any of this sound familiar?
  • the front hairline keeps receding
  • people say the crown looks sparse
  • the hair has become finer and lighter in colour
  • you have tried medication but it has not filled in as much as you wanted
Why does the hair at the back remain?

Male pattern hair loss is characterised by thinning and loss at the front and crown. Hair at the back tends to remain because it is less sensitive to the hormone that drives the loss. Hair transplantation makes use of exactly this property. Follicles from the back keep their original character and grow as before once moved (donor dominance).

How it is done — follicular unit transplantation

Hair grows in bundles of one to four (follicular units). Follicular units are separated from the back of the scalp and transplanted one by one into the area to be filled.

What surprises people most — the transplanted hair falls out

One to three weeks after surgery, the transplanted hair begins to fall. This is a normal part of the process. The follicles are alive, and the hair grows back. Knowing this in advance saves a great deal of anxiety.

1–3 weeksTransplanted hair begins to fall (normal)
3–6 monthsNew hair becomes visible
4–6 months70–90% or more grown
6–9 monthsThis is when the cosmetic result can be judged
Transplantation is not the end of it

Transplanted hair persists, but the hair that was already there can continue to fall. Medication alongside is therefore recommended after surgery to maintain the existing hair. Hair loss medicines are prescription-only and require a doctor's consultation and prescription.

What to prepare beforehand
  • Stop vitamin E, aspirin and anti-inflammatories one week before.
  • No alcohol or tobacco from two days before.
  • Wash your hair the night before and on the morning of the procedure.

Does any of this sound familiar?
  • drooping eyelids mean the lashes press into the eye
  • your field of vision is obstructed and you tense your forehead
  • puffiness under the eyes makes you look permanently tired
  • make-up will not cover the shadows under the eyes
Why does the upper eyelid age first?

The upper eyelid has the thinnest skin on the body, little subcutaneous fat, and the muscles around the eye are used more than almost any others. It is therefore one of the first places to show ageing. The problem is not only unwelcome lines: vision is obstructed and the lashes press into the eye.

Upper blepharoplasty

Surgery to correct a loose, drooping upper eyelid. An incision follows the natural crease of the eye, and as much skin, muscle and fat as necessary is removed.

This is the most important part. The cause of the droop differs from person to person. Skin alone, severely sagging muscle, or excess fat are all different, and the surgery must follow an accurate diagnosis of which it is. If the eyelid droops because of ptosis, correction for that is needed separately.

AnaesthesiaLocal
Suture removalAround four days after surgery
Return to normal lifeAbout one week for both daily and working life
Lower blepharoplasty

The lower eyelid also thins, its muscle loosens and it descends. As the membrane supporting the fat beneath the eye weakens, the fat pushes forward and forms a bulging pouch. Lower blepharoplasty removes excess fat or repositions it where there is too little, tightens the loosened membrane, and tidies loose skin and muscle.

  • Where skin and muscle are fine and only the fat bulges — surgery can be performed through an incision inside the eyelid, without cutting the skin.
  • Where the eyes are, conversely, very hollow — fat grafting can restore a younger look.
Points to be aware of
  • If you have high blood pressure or take medicines affecting blood clotting, recovery can be slower. Please tell us at the consultation.
  • Keep the pillow high and use cold packs for two to three days after surgery, and for about a week avoid watching television lying down or reading for long periods.
  • Problems under the eye arise both from too much fat and from too little. Whether to remove, to fill, or to do both can be discussed in the same appointment.

A face that looks older shows these changes
DescentHollowing (atrophy)
Elastic fibres and collagen degrade, firmness is lost and tissue descends. The cheeks drop, nasolabial folds form and the area under the chin loosensThe cheeks and the area around the eyes hollow and look gaunt. As fullness disappears, the forehead and brows appear to droop

Lifting alone can therefore be insufficient. That is why lifting treatments and filling treatments must be considered together.

What methods are there?
CategoryProcedureConsidered when
IncisionalFacelift, forehead and brow liftThe skin has descended so far that other methods are expected to be less effective
Partial incisionMini-lift, fat graftingYou want to shorten the recovery period
Non-incisionalBotulinum toxin, fillersLines caused by expression, or filling hollow areas

Surgery is usually performed between 40 and 60, but with good health a good result can be obtained at 70 or 80 as well. The result is better while some elasticity remains in the skin.

Facelift (incisional)

The most traditional method: the incision runs inside the hairline, in front of the ear and round behind it. Subcutaneous tissue, muscle and fascia are tightened and sutured, and the loose skin is trimmed. Sutures come out at five to seven days, and daily and working life are unaffected within two to three weeks. Early on, swelling may make the result unsatisfying, but most people are satisfied once time passes.

Forehead and brow lift

Deeply etched forehead lines are corrected most effectively by surgical lifting rather than by botulinum toxin or fillers. The scalp inside the hairline is opened and the forehead skin is drawn upwards; daily life is possible in about two weeks.

Micro fat grafting (a filling treatment)

Fat is harvested from the abdomen or thighs, impurities are removed, and only the pure fat is injected where needed. It restores volume to hollow areas for a softer, younger look, and lines can become less marked as a secondary effect.

  • The two to three weeks after grafting matter — this is when the fat settles, so avoid smoking and strenuous activity.
  • Some of the graft is absorbed, so slight overcorrection or a further injection may be needed.
Botulinum toxin and fillers (without incision)
  • Botulinum toxin — the effect appears after two to three days, the lines are felt to have smoothed within one to two weeks, and it lasts four to six months. It is effective for fine lines between the brows and around the eyes, and has no effect on deep lines that have already formed.
  • Fillers — substances injected to improve depressed scars, lines and facial contour. The effect appears immediately after injection and usually lasts six months to a year. Always check that the product is approved by the Korean Ministry of Food and Drug Safety.
Daily habits that slow lines
  • Keep the eye area and neck hydrated with moisturising products, and always apply sunscreen when going out.
  • Smoking reduces skin elasticity and hinders repair. Rapid weight loss makes skin sag and lines deepen.
  • Avoid always sleeping on one side, and pillows that are too high.

Does any of this sound familiar?
  • enlarged labia minora chafe and are uncomfortable when you move
  • the two sides differ in shape and this bothers you
  • hygiene is difficult to manage
  • there is pain during intercourse
What is labiaplasty?

It is performed where the labia minora are too large or asymmetrical and cause discomfort in movement, cosmetic concern, pain during intercourse or hygiene problems. The aim of surgery is to correct the shape and size without causing scarring or any abnormality of the anatomical structure.

How the surgery is done

After designing against normal size and shape, only the unnecessary portion is excised while minimising damage to nerves and vessels. It is carried out under local anaesthesia, with sedation added if needed. No special preparation is required.

Recovery
Healing period2–3 weeks
Sexual activityPossible from about 3 weeks
Points to be aware of

Possible complications include scarring at the surgical site, asymmetry of shape and size, and pain during intercourse. Please decide after a full explanation before surgery.

※ Women's surgery is a field in which the appropriate method varies greatly with individual condition. Details are explained through a medical consultation.

Frequently asked questions

Is there anything I have to stop before surgery?
Stop smoking and aspirin-type painkillers two weeks before surgery, to prevent bleeding and haematoma. This applies equally to eye, nose, breast and lifting surgery. For hair transplantation, stop vitamin E, aspirin and anti-inflammatories one week before, and alcohol and tobacco two days before.
When does the swelling go down?
It varies by area. For the eyes it is worst on days two to three and you can return to daily life within a week; for the nose, swelling and bruising can last two to three weeks. In all cases, keeping the pillow high and using cold packs for two to three days after surgery helps.
When should I judge the result?
Do not rush. A double eyelid takes two to three months, a facelift some weeks after returning to work, and a hair transplant six to nine months before it can be judged.
Will a scar remain?
It depends on the method. With an incision inside the nose no scar is visible externally, and the scar from breast reduction is in a position that does not show even when dressed and fades over several months. Rather than prioritising a method that leaves no scar, it is better to choose the method most appropriate to the procedure you need.
I am elderly — is surgery possible?
For lifting surgery the usual age range is 40 to 60, but where health allows, good results can be obtained at 70 or 80 as well.
Can one be too young?
Rhinoplasty is recommended after puberty, once the nose has taken its adult form, and breast reduction once breast growth has completely finished.
Should I mention the medicines I take?
Please do, without fail. If you have high blood pressure or take medicines affecting blood clotting, recovery can take longer. There are also cases in which botulinum toxin must not be given, and its effect can vary with the medicines you take.
Will it affect breastfeeding?
Breast augmentation does not interfere with breastfeeding. However, difficulty can arise where a very large breast has been reduced and after surgery for severely inverted nipples.

Please note

  • The content of this page is general medical information and does not replace diagnosis or a treatment plan for any individual.
  • Surgical methods, recovery periods and results can vary with age, skin condition, anatomical structure and underlying conditions.
  • All surgery carries risk, and plastic surgery is no exception. Please obtain a full explanation from your surgeon before surgery about bleeding, haematoma, infection, scarring, reduced sensation, asymmetry and the possibility of revision surgery.
  • Please decide on the method that suits you through proper consultation and examination.
